claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I need to gather some information about your situation.

Let me start with a basic question:

**How many children are you hoping to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm hoping to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're looking to claim Child Benefit for your son Alex.

Let me ask you some questions to assess your eligibility:

**Is Alex currently under 16 years old?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. That's helpful to know.

**Do you live with Alex, or are you paying towards his upkeep (such as food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me, but I do help support him financially. I contribute towards his upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex doesn't live with you but you're contributing financially towards his upkeep, I need to understand a bit more about your situation.

**How much do you currently contribute towards Alex's upkeep each week or month, and how does that compare to the current Child Benefit payment rate?**

(For context, the current Child Benefit rate is £21.15 per week for the first child and £14.05 per week for each additional child.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute £50 a week towards Alex's upkeep - so that's well above the Child Benefit rate.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful information, thank you. Since you're contributing £50 per week towards Alex's upkeep, which is well above the Child Benefit payment rate, that's a positive factor for your eligibility.

Now I need to clarify an important point:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else applied to claim Child Benefit for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good to know. I have one more important question:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Thank you for providing all that information. Let me just confirm one final detail:

**When Alex goes to live with the person he currently lives with, did that happen within the last 8 weeks, or was it longer ago than that?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh no, it's been much longer than that - it's been a few months now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me explain the situation:

According to the rules, you would normally get Child Benefit for 8 weeks after a child goes to live with someone else. However, the rules also state that you can continue to get payments for longer than 8 weeks if you make contributions to your child's upkeep by the same amount or more than the Child Benefit payment.

Since it's been several months since Alex went to live with someone else, and you're contributing £50 per week towards his upkeep (which is well above the Child Benefit rate of £21.15 per week), you should be eligible to continue receiving Child Benefit for Alex.

However, because your circumstances have changed (Alex now lives with someone else), you must contact HMRC to inform them of this situation. They will need to confirm your eligibility based on your ongoing contributions.
